title: Activity-based temporal hypergraphs: from individual activity to collective social dynamics
authors: Marco Mancastroppa, Giulia Cencetti, Iacopo Iacopini, Giovanni Petri, Alain Barrat
abstract: Temporal hypergraphs provide an interesting representation for many social systems, as they integrate both the temporal and group nature of social interactions. Designing models of time-varying hyper-networks yields thus a convenient way to generate surrogates of empirical social systems, to understand the mechanisms underlying their emergent properties, and to investigate the evolution of dynamical processes taking place on such structures. Here, we focus on a specific and powerful class of these models, the activity-based temporal hypergraphs. We show how activity mechanisms provide control over the time scale of the dynamics, allow high modelling flexibility, and capture heterogeneity in agents' behavior. We also highlight how the activity can straightforwardly be extracted from empirical data to create surrogate datasets. We present paradigmatic examples of such models: the higher-order activity-driven models (HADx), which show that different underlying rules for the selection of active interactions produce different higher-order dynamics; the Emerging Activity Temporal Hypergraph model (EATH), able to generate surrogates of empirical systems by using higher-order mechanisms driven by both activity and group memory. We conclude discussing future perspectives for activity-based temporal hypergraphs, highlighting the potential of this framework to bridge realistic modelling of social dynamics with the study of the complex dynamical process they can support, from social contagion to opinion dynamics.
summary: This paper introduces activity-based temporal hypergraphs as a powerful mathematical framework for modeling complex social dynamics. By focusing on node 'activity' rather than just network topology, the model can generate realistic synthetic data for processes like social contagion. It offers a flexible tool to study emergent collective behavior in systems with both time and group structure.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of modeling complex social systems that exhibit both temporal evolution and group interactions simultaneously.
main_result: The proposed activity-based temporal hypergraph framework (EATH) provides a highly flexible method to generate realistic surrogates of empirical social systems, applicable to processes like contagion and opinion dynamics.
method: The authors develop and compare several activity-driven models, progressing from simple activity-driven networks to higher-order activity-driven hypergraphs (HADx) and the advanced EATH model.
model_or_system: The core model is the activity-based temporal hypergraph, which represents social interactions as hyperedges evolving over time. It moves beyond simple topology-driven models by focusing on the 'activity' of individual nodes or groups.
key_observables: Higher-order dynamics, average involvement of nodes, and the ability to generate synthetic datasets mimicking empirical social structures.
important_parameters: Activity rates ($a_i$), attractiveness parameters ($b_i$), and the size distribution ($\Psi(m)$) governing hyperedge formation.
main_assumptions: The primary limitation discussed is the shift from topology-driven to node-driven dynamics, and the use of discrete-time approximations may lose fine-scale temporal information.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically illustrates temporal hypergraphs using node-centered and hyperedge-centered views. Figure 2 details the mechanics of the HAD model, showing node activation leading to hyperedge generation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the need for temporal hypergraphs, then introducing and detailing the general activity-driven models (AD $ightarrow$ HADx $ightarrow$ EATH), and finally discussing the broad applicability of this framework to various complex dynamical processes.
why_interesting: While focused on social physics, the mathematical machinery developed—modeling non-equilibrium dynamics, emergent collective behavior, and complex temporal correlations—shares conceptual overlap with modeling non-equilibrium quantum many-body systems or open quantum systems driven by external, fluctuating fields.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks

figures.caption: FIG. 1. Schematic representation of temporal hypergraphs. We show some snapshots of a temporal hypergraph, its aggregated hypergraph and the corresponding hyperedge-centered and node-centered representations, limited to nodes i, j, k, l. Note that the hyperedge-representation would require to consider all the triplets and pairs within the set {i, j, k, l}, however for simplicity we show only the hyperedges active at least once.

FIG. 2. Schematic representation of the HAD model. We schematically show the mechanisms underlying the HAD model. We consider a population of nodes of different activity, (ai - indicated with their size). (i) Over time the nodes are activated with rates equal to their activity. When active (red), they create a hyperedge whose size m is extracted from the distribution Ψ(m), and select the nodes with which to interact uniformly at random; (ii) these mechanisms generate a temporal hypergraph HAD, which can also be aggregated to obtain a static hypergraph (iii).

FIG. 3. Schematic representation of the HADA model. We schematically show the mechanisms underlying the HADA model. We consider a population of nodes of different activity and attractiveness (ai and bi = ai - indicated with their size). (i) Over time, the nodes are activated with rates equal to their activity. When active (red), they create a hyperedge whose size m is extracted from the distribution Ψ(m), and select the nodes with which to interact with probability proportional to their attractiveness b; (ii) these mechanisms generate a temporal hypergraph HADA, which can be aggregated to obtain a static hypergraph (iii).

We consider a population of nodes of different activity and attractiveness (ai and bi = ai - indicated with their size) and with an already initialized memory matrix wi,j(t) schematically represented trough a pairwise weighted network. FIG. 5. Schematic representation of the EATH model. We schematically show the generation phases of the EATH model. (i) Generation of the nodes activity dynamics, which transition between low- and high-activity states. (ii) The overall activity of the system emerges from the activity dynamics of individual nodes and from the size distribution Ψ(m). (iii) The members of active interactions are selected with memory and activity mechanisms. The selection phase (iii) generates the actual groups dynamics and node dynamics (iv).
